correctness.rationale: Every condition is defined on the full thirteen-column PG(2,3) incidence matrix. The dual complement forbids intersection size three on four-point lines. A no-five-arc parity argument and affine subspace closure classify every allowable complement into nine projective types. Their combinatorial counts prove E(z); each nonempty stopping configuration contains a six-set, and a unique two-line covering count proves every coefficient of the erasure-failure polynomial. Independently written verify.py and verify_independent.cpp exhaust all 8192 masks, agree on 769 stopping sets and 3004 peeling failures, and the Python checker additionally verifies 5616 projectivities and the nine complete orbits listed in orbits.csv. The proof is a complete finite theorem, not a sample inference; it is limited to this parity-check matrix.

originality.rationale: The order-three stopping distance six and geometric minimum-six configurations are explicitly credited to older literature. The material read from Kashyap–Vardy treats the general design framework and full enumerator for order two plus order-four partial coefficients, but not this order-three all-size classification or the exact erasure-failure polynomial. value.rationale: The precise invariant is motivated by the full stopping-set weight enumerator requested as a harder objective in the foundational design-code literature and by exact finite-length failure probability of iterative erasure decoding. The nine projective classes provide a transparent structural classification, and the all-minimum-containment/two-line cover theorem translates stopping structure into the independently useful 3004-pattern failure spectrum. It is a natural complete case for a canonical small projective plane rather than a chosen arbitrary slice. No generalization to other orders is needed for this self-contained value.
